title: Targeting H4K20 methylation to rejuvenate aged stem cell epigenome and regenerative function.
text:
In the elderly, tissue regeneration is impaired and repeated injury often precludes the health benefits of exercise. My proposal
will determine if the loss of lysine methyltransferase 5a (Kmt5a) and subsequently Kmt5a-mediated methylation of lysine
20 on histone H4 (H4K20me1) during aging disrupts muscle stem cell quiescence, consequently impairing skeletal muscle
regeneration. Data generated by this proposal will first (K99) define Kmt5a role in quiescent muscle stem cells at
homeostasis and in response to a skeletal muscle injury during aging, and then (R00) define H4K20me1 as an epigenetic
modification that can be stimulated by exercise to rejuvenate muscle and hematopoietic stem cell function in the context of
aging.

title: Molecular mechanisms in sweat gland innervation
text:
Severe burn victims and patients suffering from congenital sweat gland deficiencies are unable to properly
maintain body temperature, which can lead to hyperthermia, heat stroke, brain damage, and potentially death.
Restoring the capacity of these patients to thermoregulate requires the ability to regenerate skin with functional
sweat glands that are precisely regulated by the nervous system. This proposal will uncover novel molecular
mechanisms of neuronal control in sweat gland development, advancing our understanding of skin and sweat
gland regeneration and the development of therapeutics to treat patients with sweating deficiency.

title: Influence of DNA methylation changes on gene expression from the inactive X chromosome in B cells
text:
Several autoimmune diseases exhibit a strong female bias, but the mechanisms underlying this bias are poorly
understood. Altered X-linked gene expression in female-biased autoimmune disease patient lymphocytes
suggests gene expression from the inactive X in female cells may be dysregulated. This project aims to
investigate how changes in DNA methylation, which is globally dysregulated in patient cells, impact gene
expression from the inactive X chromosome in B cells, and whether DNA methylation regulates gene
expression independently of Xist, the long non-coding RNA responsible for X chromosome inactivation.

title: Decoding Functional Cell-Cell Communication to Uncover Cellular State Modulation, Tissue Homeostasis, and Disease Genetics
text:
8. PROJECT NARRATIVE
The proposed research is relevant to public health as it aims to develop advanced computational methods to
systematically decode functional cell-cell communication, a key factor in maintaining tissue homeostasis and
understanding disease mechanisms. Once these methodologies are established, they hold the potential to
revolutionize our understanding of complex genetic diseases and uncover novel therapeutic targets. Therefore,
this research aligns with the NIH’s mission to improve health, extend life, and reduce illness and disability by
advancing our comprehension of fundamental biological processes and their implications for human well-being.

title: Deciphering the contribution of the aged alveolar niche to lung cancer evolution
text:
The exponential increase in the older population globally is inextricably linked to the exponential increase of
many-age related diseases including cancer, the most lethal age-related disease and whose incidence increases
11-fold as a function of old age. Despite this, and contrary to other age-related diseases such as Alzheimer’s or
diabetes, currently only a very small proportion of cancer studies factor in the aging process. Here, we put
forward aging as a key driver of lung cancer evolution determining evolution of specific cancer cell populations
that confer poor prognosis upon treatment and to identify novel therapeutic strategies for older cancer patients
that factors in the reprogramming that occurs with aging.

title: Nuclear import receptors as modifiers of TDP-43 phase transition and toxicity in FTD/ALS
text:
The mislocalization and abnormal aggregation of the protein TDP-43 is a hallmark of pathology in the related neurodegenerative diseases amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), which is an Alzheimer’s disease related dementia (ADRD). Pathological aggregates of insoluble TDP-43 protein are also commonly found in Alzheimer’s disease 
and other devastating disorders. Here we propose to study how specific nuclear-import receptor proteins (importins) can act as molecular chaperones that restore solubility, nuclear localization, and normal function to TDP-43, and prevent neurodegeneration in cellular and animal models of FTD and ALS.

title: Asymptomatic TB Transmission, Infectiousness, and Immunology
text:
Tuberculosis (TB) is the leading infectious disease-related cause of death and is spread person-to-person by
breathing in infectious particles. Interrupting the transmission chain requires the early diagnosis and treatment
of persons with TB, including those with asymptomatic TB. This proposal will investigate asymptomatic TB,
including infectiousness and transmission, disease trajectories, pathogenesis, and tools for its early detection
based on personal device monitoring and machine learning models.

title: Automated lung sound analysis to improve the clinical diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis in children
text:
Tuberculosis (TB) is a major cause of childhood mortality globally, and novel point-of-care tools are needed to
support earlier diagnosis and rapid TB treatment initiation in lower-level health facilities. This study will develop
and initially validate artificial-intelligence (AI) models that utilize lung sounds to automatically detect lower airway
abnormalities and TB in children, alone and in combination with clinical data included in TB treatment decision
algorithms. If successful, this would support the integration of AI-based digital health tools into clinical care to
increase the early detection and treatment of TB and other respiratory diseases in children.

title: Data Management & Bioformatics Core
text:
BDM CORE NARRATIVE
The primary functions of the Bioinformatic and Data Management (BDM) Core are to provide 1) data
management, 2) bioinformatic and 3) biostatistical analysis support to all the Projects and Cores of this
program. The Core is required for proper analysis of data generated within each project, for networking of data
across projects for complex analyses by the Computational & Predictive Modeling Core (CPM), and for
ensuring the NIH-funded research data is findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (i.e., the FAIR
principles). Services will be provided in the following areas:
 · Data monitoring and management.
 · Database infrastructure and storage.
 · Data upload into public domain repositories.
 · Development and implementation of bioinformatics tools and software to create a central data
 processing platform of high throughput biological data.
 · Selection of study populations using judicious matching algorithms for enhanced reproducibility of
 results and mitigation of confounded conclusions.
 · Biostatistical design and standard analysis of project studies.
 · Assistance with manuscript preparation.
 · Education and career development.

title: Leveraging Context-Specific eQTL to Inform BMD GWAS
text:
Osteoporosis is a major public health burden, and a condition characterized by decreased bone mineral
density (BMD). Current estimates indicate that 12 million people suffer from osteoporosis in the U.S.
Osteoporosis is largely influenced by genetics. This project seeks to identify specific genes influencing BMD
and osteoporosis using an innovative systems genetics analysis. Successful completion of this project will
identify new therapeutic targets for the treatment of osteoporosis.

title: Mechanisms of fibrosis and remodeling in arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse
text:
Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) has been increasingly linked to life-threatening arrhythmias, yet the biomechanical
mechanisms driving arrhythmogenesis in MVP remain poorly understood, limiting effective risk stratification
and early intervention. This research will address a critical gap in mechanistic understanding by leveraging
high-fidelity cardiac imaging and patient-specific computational modeling to reveal the mechanical and
hemodynamic factors contributing to MVP-associated arrhythmias. Building on these insights, we will elucidate
MRI-derived predictive biomarkers to provide non-invasive, precision-medicine metrics for early risk
stratification and personalized clinical management of MVP patients.

title: Knowledge Augmented AI for Precision Surveillance and Control of Hospital-Acquired Infections
text:
This project will develop a new robust and generalizable methodology for HAI risk prediction and surveil-
lance, which will be implemented using federated learning across six hospitals, effectively using the largest HAI
dataset ever studied. An Infection Prevention Operations Dashboard will be developed and evaluated at two
hospital systems.

title: Understanding Cell Behavior in Precise Multifunctional Biomimetic Matrices Prepared via 3D Printing
text:
Modern medicine relies on our ability to effectively interface synthetic materials with biology to facilitate disease
monitoring, diagnosis, and treatment. The contemporary reliance on monolithic 2D cell culture fails to capture
the complex, 3D biological environment and thus precludes our ability to accurately study cell behavior and
manage illness. The proposed research addresses this grand challenge through creating novel multifunctional
matrices via color- and intensity-selective 3D bioprinting of tissue mimetics and directly studying cellular
responses to local changes in shape, stiffness, and chemical signals within them.

title: Post-transcriptional control of cyclin expression during cell division
text:
Cyclins activate cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) to drive cell cycle progression, and cyclin expression must be
tightly regulated to ensure accurate cell cycle transitions. The proposed research will investigate how cyclin 3’
untranslated regions (UTRs) are post-transcriptionally regulated to control cyclin expression during cell division.
Investigating these mechanisms will improve our understanding of cell cycle control and provide insights into
how cyclin misexpression drives human diseases such as cancer, infertility, miscarriage, and trisomy conditions.

title: Signal-Induced Regulation of Alternative RNA Processing
text:
Relevance
To function appropriately and prevent disease states, all cells in the human body must be able to regulate
what proteins they make in response to environmental cues or need. RNA processing, including alternative
splicing, polyadenylation and regulated protein synthesis, are pervasive mechanisms for regulating protein
expression and cellular function in response to extracellular triggers. The studies in this proposal seek to
elucidate the regulatory pathways and molecular mechanisms by which changes in environment regulate
RNA processing, and to determine the consequences of such regulation for maintaining proper cellular
function and human health.

title: Dissecting MCPyV ALTO transcription and tumor suppression
text:
Merkel cell carcinoma is a deadly type of skin cancer caused primarily by Merkel cell polyomavirus and has
limited treatment options. One of the Merkel virus genes (ALTO) is turned off in Merkel cancer and turning it
back on switches off the viral genes (LT and ST) that cause cancer, making the cancer cells stop growing. The
proposed studies will reveal how ALTO can be turned on, how ALTO turns off LT and ST, and how ALTO helps
the immune system to recognize and kill Merkel cancer cells, providing insights that could aid the development
of new treatments for Merkel cell cancer in the future.

title: An aberrant wound healing response drives myeloid-dependent disease exacerbation
text:
Chronic inflammatory conditions ranging from cancer to autoimmunity and infection all exhibit an Spp1+
macrophage response, which strongly correlates with poor outcomes. However, as this macrophage population
has only recently been identified, the drivers of its differentiation and how it contributes to disease exacerbation
are unknown. The goal of this project is to leverage novel mouse models and an in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 screening
approach to define fundamental aspects of Spp1+ macrophage biology, thereby identifying novel therapeutic
targets for deadly inflammatory diseases, such as tuberculosis and head and neck cancer.

title: Direct and Indirect Neurogenesis in the Mammalian Neocortex
text:
This project will use advanced genomic, molecular and in vivo studies to compare neural
precursor cells throughout the neurogenetic period of the mouse and how the neurons they
produce contribute to the mature cortical circuitry.

title: Optimizing Optogenetics for Cell-type-specific Control in Freely-moving Primates
text:
Optogenetics is a powerful technique for modulating precisely selected neural circuits, but despite having
numerous research and therapeutic applications, achieving neuromodulation that significantly impacts behavior
in primates has proved challenging. Here we develop new optogenetic expression and stimulation techniques to
achieve this goal in freely behaving primates. This will allow us to better study and develop translational therapies
targeting the neural circuitry underlying a variety of neurological and psychiatric disorders in human populations.

title: Determining factors of inflammation that support the expansion and function of long-lived effector cell CD8 T cells in a mature memory compartment
text:
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
Traditional SPF mouse models do not accurately reflect the immune compartment makeup observed in
humans, particularly the T cell compartment. This proposal utilizes pet store mouse cohousing to normalize
mouse pathogen exposure with the goal to explore the maintenance and function of long-lived effector CD8 T
cells. These studies will help better understand the factors that promote T cell maintenance and function in a
model with normal levels of pathogen exposure.
